editorial:
Imagine you are Mitsuhiko, a guy working as an assistant director who thinks he is in total control of his life. He decides to hire a young call girl for a quick hotel visit, but things get messy fast. He starts paying her 30,000 yen per date, thinking he is just buying some company and intimacy. However, you will quickly see that he is not the one calling the shots. The vibe starts out as a simple arrangement, but it slowly turns into a psychological game where the girl holds all the power. It is a wild ride that shows how a simple transaction can spiral into something much more dangerous.

What really hits home is how the power dynamic shifts throughout the story. The acting is solid, and you can feel the tension grow as Mitsuhiko realizes he is being played. While the pacing starts a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy movies about obsession and manipulation, you should definitely check this one out. To get the best experience, try renting it on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for those crisp visuals. It is a great pick for a late-night movie session when you want something that keeps you guessing.
endingExplained: In the end, you see that the girl was never truly in love with Mitsuhiko. She used his feelings and his money to get exactly what she wanted. The twist reveals that she was manipulating him from the very start to secure her own future. Mitsuhiko is left broken and empty, realizing he was just a paycheck to her. He ends up losing his grip on his life while she moves on without any guilt.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological dramas about toxic relationships.
